{"type": "input_text", "text": "{\"part\":2,\"chunk_id\":\"dce098\",\"wall_time_seconds\":7.91e-7,\"exit_code\":0,\"original_token_count\":4202,\"output\":\"# Opinion\\n\\nA journalistic debate article that argues a clear position and asks for a change or a considered stance. The author takes responsibility for the argument rather than observing it from outside.\\n\\nApply the shared [web craft brief](../web-craft.md).\\n\\nFollow the [article anatomy](../article-anatomy.md).\\n\\nWrite the headline and the subheadings as [Headlines](../headlines.md) says.\\n\\n## What this genre asks for\\n\\nState the thesis early and identify its holder when an author is supplied. Let the headline and useful subheadings carry the issue and argument for a scanning reader.\\n\\nBuild a case the reader can follow, distinguishing evidence, judgement and inference. Attribute load-bearing factual claims where they are used, and meet relevant real objections fairly. Neither an argument quota nor an invented opponent makes the case stronger.\\n\\nKeep a persuasive, accountable voice without strengthening or weakening the author's supplied positions: absence of opposition is not endorsement. Criticise ideas, decisions and actions precisely; do not invent an opponent's motives. Preserve warranted sharpness as well as material qualifications, without compulsory softening or inflated rhetoric.\\n\\nThe call to action is the specific change or stance the argument supports, and the ending makes clear who can act. Reconsidering or declining a proposal can be the action; a generic exhortation alone is not one.\\n\\n## The technique this genre is ordinarily written with\\n\\nNone.\\n# Delivery\\n\\nEvery Skill that produces a Text Artifact delivers it the same way. This document is the complete contract: where a result goes, how a response carries the text, what the response carries when it went somewhere else, when a source file may be replaced instead, what happens when nothing changed, what language a run's own words about the text are written in and whether what those words say is true of the text they name, and what is refused before anything is written. It is a reference several Skills read rather than a runtime of its own. Each Skill exposes these rules through its own Formal Invocation and owns the names it gives them, so nothing here fixes how an option is spelled; what is fixed is the behaviour behind it.\\n\\n## The response is the default\\n\\nThe default Output Target is the agent response. A run that keeps the default delivers the complete Text Artifact in the response and changes nothing on the filesystem: it creates no file, touches no file, and makes no directory. That includes scratch files and working copies of the artifact, wherever the Harness says temporary files belong.\\n\\nA Harness convention identifies where an authorized temporary file belongs; it does not authorize a write. If a run genuinely needs a scratch file while composing, it removes that file before delivery and restores the filesystem to the state in which it found it. Before reporting delivery, the run checks the filesystem locations it used, including the Harness scratch area, and never reports that nothing was written while a copy of the artifact remains on disk.\\n\\nAn Output Target is independent of where the source material came from. Supplying a local file as source material selects no destination, and a run that reads a file still delivers to the response until the caller names somewhere else. Persisting a result is the caller's explicit choice, and making that choice is the whole of the authorization for it.\\n\\n## How a response carries the text\\n\\nA response carries a Text Artifact inside a fenced code block rather than as prose of the reply's own. A text and the words about it are two different things, and a reply that runs them together hands the reader a text nothing marks the edges of. Markdown is where that costs most: an artifact opening on a frontmatter delimiter, set directly beneath a paragraph the run wrote, turns that paragraph into a heading unless a blank line goes in between them — and a blank line there is what ends the frontmatter block the text was settled with. A fence removes the question rather than leaving each run to answer it, and the answers a run improvises are what made one saved reply in sixteen deliver a horizontal rule and a paragraph of configuration in place of a frontmatter block.\\n\\nThe complete Text Artifact sits inside exactly one fenced code block, byte for byte as the run settled it: frontmatter, blank lines and trailing structure included. Nothing is added, dropped or re-wrapped between the fence lines, and one block rather than several, a text split across two fences being a text the reader has to reassemble.\\n\\nThe fence is longer than the longest run of backticks inside the artifact, so a text carrying fenced code of its own cannot close it early. The info string names the text's format: `markdown` for a Markdown text, `html` for HTML, `text` for plain text.\\n\\nEverything the run says *about* the text sits outside the fence — the resolved configuration, the findings and which of them are unresolved, the claim account, where a technique came from, what the run could not do. Nothing of the run's own is inside it. What the run settled as part of the document does belong inside, the Handoff Metadata and any marking the user asked to have placed in the document itself among it, because that is the text as delivered rather than a remark about it.\\n\\nThe rule reaches every complete text a reply carries, whether this contract calls that text delivered or not. A response-targeted run that changed nothing and has findings left fences the artifact like any other; a run that stopped before it could deliver and carries its preserved prose in the reply fences that prose, and says in its own words outside the fence what the prose has not been through. The short no-change status carries no text at all and so carries no fence. An explicit destination and In-place Editing receive the text itself and never a fence: a fence is how a reply holds a text apart from its own words, and a file has no words of its own to be held apart from.\\n\\n## An explicit destination\\n\\nAn explicit destination is one filesystem path, and what exists at that path decides what happens to it.\\n\\n**A path that does not exist** creates exactly that one file and writes the complete Text Artifact into it. Exactly one file: nothing else is created beside it, and no directory is made to hold it.\\n\\n**A path naming an existing file** overwrites that exact file with the complete Text Artifact. No confirmation and no separate force option is required, and none is offered. Naming the path is the authorization, and demanding a second gesture on top of it would teach that naming a destination means something less than it says.\\n\\n**A path naming an existing directory** delivers into that directory under a filename the run derives, by the rules below. Choosing a directory selects a place, not a file, so it never overwrites a file already in it.\\n\\n## Deriving a filename for a directory\\n\\nA directory destination needs a name, and the name comes from what the run already knows. Take the first of these the run has: the basename of the local file that supplied the Text Artifact, the title of a referenced URL, then the Skill's own working title for the text it created. Reduce it to a name the filesystem accepts, and keep a suitable text extension — the source file's own where it had one, and otherwise the one matching the text's format.\\n\\nThat gives a stem and an extension, and the stem stays as it is for every delivery into that directory. Where nothing exists at the derived name, that name is the file written. Where something exists there, the existing file is never overwritten: keep the original stem and take the first free numbered candidate in ascending order, beginning at `-2`. So `my-file.md`, `my-file-2.md`, `my-file-3.md` are one sequence, growing by one name at a time.\\n\\nA numbered candidate is never adopted as the new stem. A third delivery into a directory already holding the first two is `my-file-3.md` and never `my-file-2-2.md`, whose stem would fork the sequence in two and leave the directory recording how many times the same text arrived rather than which arrival it was. Ascending order with the first free name also means a number freed by a deleted file is used again before a higher one is taken.\\n\\n## What the response carries when a destination was named\\n\\nA run that delivers to an explicit destination does not repeat the Text Artifact in the response. The response says where the text went — the derived filename included, where the destination was a directory — and carries what the file cannot: the findings the run reports beside the text, and which of them are unresolved. Naming a destination is saying where the text goes, and printing it again spends output on what the caller is already holding, doubly so when the file just written holds it too.\\n\\nThat holds whether or not the pass changed anything. A run that writes a file byte-identical to the source it read reports the destination and says the text needed no work, and does not become the one run that echoes a text the caller had before it started. The response is the default target precisely because a run that names no destination has nowhere else to put the artifact; naming one moves the text out of the response rather than duplicating it there.\\n\\n## In-place Editing\\n\\nIn-place Editing replaces the single local file that supplied the Text Artifact with the result, instead of delivering it anywhere else. It is available only to a Skill whose work is to return a changed version of a text the caller already has.\\n\\nA Skill that creates a new Text Artifact never edits its own source material in place. The brief, the interview, the notes, and the article it draws on are where the text came from and not where it goes; a Skill that could overwrite them would make supplying a file a risk rather than a convenience, and would lose the material the result is answerable to.\\n\\nIn-place Editing requires exactly one writable local source file, and it is mutually exclusive with a separate output option. A run replaces its source or delivers elsewhere, never both, and an invocation asking for both has named two destinations for one text.\\n\\nIt is refused wherever there is no such file to replace. Text supplied inline in the invocation or taken from the conversation is not a file. A URL is not a local file, and fetching one grants no right to write anything back. An uploaded source and a read-only file cannot be replaced. More than one Text Artifact leaves the single file the contract is written around undefined.\\n\\nAn explicit output path equal to the input path is refused in favour of In-place Editing, and the refusal says which gesture to use. Replacing a source then has one recognizable authorization: a reader of an invocation sees that a source is about to be replaced from the request itself, without comparing two paths to discover it.\\n\\n## When nothing changed\\n\\nA run may finish with nothing to change, and what it does then follows its destination.\\n\\nA response-targeted run that changed nothing returns a short no-change status in place of the text when no unresolved findings remain. When findings remain, deliver the complete Text Artifact in the response and report the unresolved findings separately.\\n\\nAn in-place run that changed nothing leaves the source file untouched and returns the short status with any unresolved findings. Rewriting a file with its own contents would make its timestamp claim that something happened.\\n\\nThat status is written in the language of the Text Artifact rather than the language of the invocation, so a Swedish text that needed no work is reported on in Swedish.\\n\\nAn explicitly selected different file or directory still receives the complete Text Artifact when nothing changed. Creating that artifact is what was asked for, and a destination left empty because the text needed no work is a request refused without saying so. A directory destination derives its filename and resolves collisions exactly as it would for a changed text, and the response reports the destination without repeating the artifact beside it, exactly as for a run that changed something.\\n\\n## The language of a report about the text\\n\\nA run that reports on the text beside the text itself — the findings it carries forward, and which of them are unresolved — writes that report in the language of the Text Artifact rather than the language of the invocation, exactly as the no-change status above is written. So a Swedish artifact reviewed from an English-language invocation comes back with Swedish findings, whether the run corrected anything or was asked to correct nothing at all, and one text never produces a status in its own language beside a finding list in another.\\n\\nWho reads it is what decides this. A report about a text is read by the reader of that text, who has to finish whatever the run left undone, and a report in whichever language the invocation happened to be written in reaches that reader in a language nothing about the text promised. The invocation's language is how the run was asked for; the artifact's language is what the run is about.\\n\\n## The truth of a report about the text\\n\\nEverything a run says about a text is true of the text it names. That holds for every statement the reply makes about a text, and not only for its findings and its account of the claims: a count, a length, a grammatical label, where a passage stands, and what a round did to a passage — moved it, removed it, replaced it, set a heading over it — each tells the reader something about the text they could check, and each is written so that the check holds.\\n\\nA statement about the delivered text is checked against the delivered text after the last change to it, the closing mechanical pass included. Most of what a run knows about a text it learned while reviewing the text as it arrived, and the rounds changed that text afterwards, so a length measured before a round or a heading remembered from one describes a text the reader is no longer holding. Where a run measures a text with the Collection Library's measuring script, `scripts/article_anatomy.py`, a count or length the reply states is taken from that script's measurement of the text the statement is about, never from the run's own reading of it and never from a measurement of another state of the text. A statement about the text as it arrived says so, so that nobody reads it against the text delivered. A statement that cannot be made true of the text it names is left out.\\n\\nThe check is made on the reply as drafted, one statement at a time, once the text it describes is final, and each statement is read against the passage it names rather than against what the run remembers of it; a finding written during the review is checked in the same way against the text it was written about. A statement that something holds everywhere or nowhere — that a passage is unchanged, word for word what it was or untouched, that the rest of the text was left alone, that a name appears nowhere else, that a heading says nothing about its section — is checked against every part of the text it covers, because a single exception makes it false, and where there is one the statement names it or is narrowed to what holds. A statement of where wording came from, or of where a passage now stands, is checked by finding that passage in the text.\\n\\nWho reads it decides this too. The reader of a report finds their way in the text by it, and a statement they check and find false costs them the trust they would have given every other statement in the same reply.\\n\\n## Refusals\\n\\nEvery contradictory, meaningless, or unusable output request is refused before the first side effect. The cases this contract names are more than one Text Artifact where the Skill processes one, an output option together with In-place Editing, an output path equal to the input path, In-place Editing for inline text or a URL or an uploaded or read-only source, and a destination the run cannot write — a path whose parent directory does not exist among them.\\n\\nEvery such check that can be made by reading is made before anything is written, so a refusal leaves no partial effect behind: no file created, none truncated, none renamed, and no directory made. Where a conflict can only be discovered after a legitimate effect, the run stops there and reports the exact partial outcome rather than continuing.\\n\\nA refusal follows the Collection's ordinary diagnostic and help conventions. It names what was wrong, prints the synopsis of the most specific recognized command page verbatim, and points at that command's own help form. An output option is refused rather than ignored where it has no work to do, a flag accepted and ignored teaching that flags sometimes do nothing.\\n\"}"}], "internal_chat_message_metadata_passthrough": {"turn_id": "01a0f746-c0d6-7bd0-8143-630450bece1f", "create_time": 1790855058.866992}}}

It states a strong claim plainly and lets the claim carry the emphasis, where American register would reach for an intensifier. Irony and litotes are available and are not read as evasion.\\\\n\\\\nCollective nouns take plural agreement when the members are acting and singular when the body is acting as one: *the team are arguing about it*, *the committee has published its report*. Both are correct; what matters is that the choice is consistent within a passage.\\\\n\\\\nThe present perfect covers a recent past that still bears on now: *I've just seen the figures*, *have you eaten?* The simple past in those positions reads as American.\\\\n\\\\n*Have got* is ordinary British usage for possession and obligation — *I've got the file*, *you've got to see this* — and is not an informality to be edited out of general prose.\\\\n\\\\nPrepositions differ in a small, fixed set of places: *at the weekend*, *in hospital*, *different from* or *different to*, *write to somebody*, *meet somebody* rather than *meet with*. None of these is a preference; each is the British form.\\\\n\\\\nSpelling is *-ise* or *-ize* by house style — both are correct British English, *-ise* being the majority convention and *-ize* the Oxford one — but a document uses one throughout. The *-yse* group is invariant: *analyse*, *paralyse*, *catalyse*, in Oxford spelling as in any other.\\\\n\\\\nQuotation marks are single as the outer mark in most British house styles, with double inside; some publications invert this. Follow the document's own choice and make it consistent.\\\"\\n    }\\n  }\\n}\\n\"}"}, {"type": "input_text", "text": "{\"part\":1,\"chunk_id\":\"710a32\",\"wall_time_seconds\":0.000002333,\"exit_code\":0,\"original_token_count\":7217,\"output\":\"# The base contract\\n\\nWrite with the clarity and factual precision of a well-edited newspaper or quality magazine. Genre, audience, and purpose override that register: a letter, a speech and an advertisement keep their own character. The selected genre governs craft and form; the resolved language governs idiom, syntax and typography. Examples here illustrate meanings, not English phrases to translate.\\n\\n## Reader and progression\\n\\nGive the intended reader what they need to understand, judge or do the thing the text is for. Keep a clear focus, introduce unfamiliar concepts before the reasoning needs them, and order material by that reader's needs rather than the writer's discovery process. Relevant technical detail belongs; unexplained jargon and unrelated background do not.\\n\\nMake the relations between passages real. A transition may explain a connection, but cannot invent one. Keep paragraphs coherent and give supporting material a clear place beside what it supports. The body and its sections remain intelligible without treating a title, standfirst or subheading as their opening sentence.\\n\\nOpen on something specific to the subject. End with what the job calls for: an earned understanding, conclusion, recommendation or next step. Remove introductions and conclusions that add only an announcement or a generic flourish.\\n\\n## Expression\\n\\nUse concrete words, useful verbs and a natural, varied cadence. Keep terminology and reference clear; introduce an unfamiliar abbreviation before using it alone. Choose ordinary words where they suffice and established specialist terms where they give this reader precision.\\n\\nLet tone and rhetorical devices serve the genre and the meaning. A useful analogy, question, image, fragment or humorous turn can clarify or carry a voice; decoration and manufactured drama cannot. An imagined comparison is recognisable as a comparison, never presented as an event or someone's experience. Criticism addresses the supported issue without inventing motives or patronising the reader.\\n\\nEach passage earns its place. Repetition may establish an independent entry point, explain a hard idea or give a deliberate rhetorical return; merely saying the same thing again does none of these. Keep formatting useful: headings for orientation, lists for coordinate items, tables for comparisons, emphasis for what merits it. Hold voice, terminology and presentation consistent unless a visible purpose calls for a change.\\n\\n## Claims\\n\\nEvery claim is supported by the text or its material, with exact attribution and proportionate strength. Preserve the state of knowledge: what is unknown or unclaimed is not thereby known not to have happened. Keep uncertainty where it exists and certainty where it is warranted. A fact, quotation, source, scene, personal experience or opinion attributed to somebody is never invented to complete a form. Name the actual source of an attributed claim rather than invoking unnamed studies or experts.\\n\\nCircumstantial detail is a claim too: duration, manner, motive, absence and background all need support. So does an evaluative characterisation: calling a count high, low or modest needs a comparison, target, capacity or speaker assessment. Otherwise give the count with its exclusions, without that assessment.\\n\\nA sequence or correlation establishes no cause. A causal verb such as *shortened* needs causal support; a causal hedge such as *suggests that it shortened* still adds that attribution. This boundary holds in the title, summary, headings and body alike. Preserve chronology, scope and qualifications wherever a claim appears.\\n\\nA stated length constrains the use of material and is never a licence to add to it. When the material is insufficient, deliver the length the material supports and name what further material would close the gap. A supplied publication limit is binding; meeting it cannot justify invention or loss of a qualification that changes a claim.\\n# Craft for five web genres\\n\\nFor article, casestudy, column and opinion, work as a skilled Swedish journalist at the professional level of SvD, DN, DI, Fokus, Ny Teknik, Filter or Forskning & Framsteg. For webcopy, work as an experienced Swedish copywriter and UX writer trusted by leading agencies and brands. These are standards of craft, not voices to imitate.\\n\\nIn every target language, keep that Swedish editorial or communicative tradition in the angle, disposition, storytelling, address and tone. Think and write wholly in the target language: its Language Resource governs vocabulary, idiom, syntax, punctuation and typography. A native professional should hear a colleague, not a translation. Language choice changes the language surface, not the chosen craft.\\n\\n## Web reading\\n\\nGive the reader a clear angle or task and useful ways into the text. Let facts and reasoning carry explanation; choose any narrative devices for what they contribute. Headings orient according to the genre, paragraphs hold connected thoughts, and varied rhythm supports both scanning and sustained reading.\\n\\nFor article, casestudy, column and opinion, the [article anatomy](article-anatomy.md) fixes the parts, their order and their dimensions.\\n# Article anatomy\\n\\nThe fixed skeleton of a text in the genres `article`, `casestudy`, `column` and `opinion`; *article* below means a text in any of them. The anatomy fixes which parts the text has, their order and their dimensions. Angle, argument, voice and language are outside it.\\n\\nA statement below has one of three strengths:\\n\\n- A plain statement is a requirement: it holds in every conforming text.\\n- *Should* marks a norm: follow it as a requirement, and depart only when following it is impossible or the departure is clearly better for the reader.\\n- *Most* states what is typical across the whole text; each single paragraph or section follows its own content.\\n\\nA text conforms when every part is present in the order shown and all three hold. Limits are exact; verify each one by counting.\\n\\nA review of a finished text reports a part the text lacks as missing rather than writing it, and repairs only the parts the text has.\\n\\n## Order\\n\\n```text\\nHeadline\\nStandfirst\\nByline\\nLead\\nSubheading        ┐ a section; one or more\\nParagraphs        ┘\\nLast subheading   ┐ the ending\\nParagraphs        ┘\\n```\\n\\nEach part appears once, except the section, which repeats. The first subheading follows the lead directly. The body is everything from the lead through the ending.\\n\\nThe headline is the text's level-1 heading (HTML `h1`, Markdown `#`), and every subheading is a level-2 heading (HTML `h2`, Markdown `##`). The text should use these two levels only. Where an academic text would nest a level-3 heading, a further level-2 subheading usually serves; a level-3 heading is for the rare text whose structure truly demands one.\\n\\n## Headline\\n\\n- 20–70 characters, spaces included.\\n- It should be three to eight words and at most 60 characters.\\n- It is written as [Headlines](headlines.md) says.\\n\\n## Standfirst\\n\\nThe standfirst is a summarising paragraph that introduces the article and stands on its own. Förvaltningens verkliga invändning mot att behålla båda kanalerna är dubbel administration, inte att telefonanvändare är lata eller dyra.

Öppna beslut föreslår ett sex månader långt försök i alla sju lokaler, med båda bokningsvägarna kvar. Under försöket ska förvaltningen registrera tidsåtgång per bokningsväg och be användarna frivilligt ange varför de väljer telefon eller webb. Föreningen gör inget anspråk på att ha finansierat eller kostnadsberäknat försöket. Kostnaden behöver kommunstyrelsen ta ställning till. Därefter kan den avgöra om en kanal ska tas bort, ändras eller behållas.

Sanna Eks ståndpunkt: ”Att en bokning går via telefon är inte ett bevis för att någon inte kan använda webben. Det är ett skäl att ta reda på varför telefonen fortfarande används.” Detta får citeras eller refereras. Hon menar att kommunen först måste kunna väga arbetskostnaden mot värdet för användarna. Hon motsätter sig inte digital bokning.

Inga lagkrav, protester, diskrimineringsfall, partipolitiska motiv eller besparingar är belagda. Siffror ska tillskrivas rapporten där de bär argumentet. ## Underlag

Kommunens pilotrapport Bokning av föreningslokaler, 8 april 2026, gäller ett åtta veckor långt försök i två lokaler. Under försöket gjordes 96 bokningar via webb och 24 via telefon. Rapporten räknar bokningar, inte unika personer. Den mäter inte ålder, funktionsförmåga eller digital vana. Telefonbokningarna kan därför inte användas för att säga hur stor andel av invånarna som inte kan boka digitalt.

Tjänsteutlåtandet inför kommunstyrelsens möte den 18 juni föreslår att telefonbokning tas bort för alla sju lokaler från september. Motivet i utlåtandet är att personalen ska slippa föra in uppgifter i två flöden. Någon tidsmätning eller ekonomisk besparingsberäkning finns inte i handlingarna. Förvaltningens verkliga invändning mot att behålla båda kanalerna är dubbel administration, inte att telefonanvändare är lata eller dyra.

Öppna beslut föreslår ett sex månader långt försök i alla sju lokaler, med båda bokningsvägarna kvar. Under försöket ska förvaltningen registrera tidsåtgång per bokningsväg och be användarna frivilligt ange varför de väljer telefon eller webb. Föreningen gör inget anspråk på att ha finansierat eller kostnadsberäknat försöket. Kostnaden behöver kommunstyrelsen ta ställning till. Därefter kan den avgöra om en kanal ska tas bort, ändras eller behållas.

Sanna Eks ståndpunkt: ”Att en bokning går via telefon är inte ett bevis för att någon inte kan använda webben. Det är ett skäl att ta reda på varför telefonen fortfarande används.” Detta får citeras eller refereras. Hon menar att kommunen först måste kunna väga arbetskostnaden mot värdet för användarna. # Lervik needs evidence before ending telephone bookings

The case for removing telephone bookings from Lervik’s association premises rests on avoiding duplicate administration. But the papers provide no measurement of staff time or calculated savings. The municipal executive board should establish what each route costs and why people use it.

By Sanna Ek, spokesperson for Öppna beslut

A staff report for the 18 June meeting of Lervik’s municipal executive board proposes ending telephone booking at all seven association premises from September. Öppna beslut wants that permanent switch postponed while both telephone and web booking are tested for six months. I do not oppose digital booking; I question whether the evidence justifies removing the alternative.

## The pilot figures leave users’ reasons unanswered

The municipality’s pilot report, Booking Association Premises, dated 8 April 2026, records 96 web bookings and 24 telephone bookings during an eight-week trial at two venues. Those figures describe bookings, not unique individuals.

It did not measure age, functional ability or familiarity with digital technology. We cannot use the telephone bookings to calculate how many residents cannot book online. A booking made by telephone proves no inability to use the web; it gives us a reason to ask why that route is still used.

## Duplicate administration deserves a fair assessment

The administration wants staff to avoid entering information through two workflows. That objection deserves to be taken seriously. Its case concerns duplicate administration, not a claim that telephone users are lazy or costly.

Yet the papers contain neither a measurement of staff time nor a calculation of financial savings. Before making a permanent change, the board should be able to weigh the labour cost against the value for users. The pilot’s booking totals cannot settle that judgement.

## A wider trial can inform the decision

Our proposal covers all seven venues for six months, keeping both booking routes.

Staff would record the time spent on each route and ask users to explain their choice voluntarily. This would help the board assess both the workload and users’ reasons.

## The board should postpone the permanent switch

Öppna beslut makes no claim to have funded or costed the trial. The executive board must consider its cost, postpone the permanent switch and first test both routes. It can then decide whether a booking channel should be removed, changed or retained.

# Lervik needs evidence before ending telephone bookings

The case for removing telephone bookings from Lervik’s association premises rests on avoiding duplicate administration. But the papers provide no measurement of staff time or calculated savings. The municipal executive board should establish what each route costs and why people use it.

By Sanna Ek, spokesperson for Öppna beslut

A staff report for the 18 June meeting of Lervik’s municipal executive board proposes ending telephone booking at all seven premises for local associations from September. Öppna beslut wants that permanent switch postponed while both telephone and web booking are tested for six months. I do not oppose digital booking; I question whether the evidence justifies removing the alternative.

## The pilot leaves users’ reasons unanswered

The municipality’s pilot report, Booking Association Premises, dated 8 April 2026, records 96 web bookings and 24 telephone bookings during an eight-week trial at two venues. Those figures describe bookings, not unique individuals.

It did not measure age, functional ability or familiarity with digital technology. We cannot use the telephone bookings to calculate how many residents cannot book online. A booking made by telephone proves no inability to use the web; it gives us a reason to ask why that route is still used.

## Duplicate administration deserves a fair assessment

The administration wants staff to avoid entering information through two workflows. That objection deserves to be taken seriously. Its case concerns duplicate administration, not a claim that telephone users are lazy or costly.

Yet the papers contain neither a measurement of staff time nor a calculation of financial savings. Before making a permanent change, the board should be able to weigh the work involved against the value for users. The pilot’s booking totals cannot settle that judgement.

## A wider trial can inform the decision

Our proposal covers all seven venues for six months, keeping both booking routes.

Staff would record the time spent on each route and ask users to explain their choice voluntarily. This would help the board assess both the workload and users’ reasons.

## The board should postpone the permanent switch

Öppna beslut makes no claim to have funded or costed the trial. The executive board must consider its cost, postpone the permanent switch and first test both routes. It can then decide whether a booking channel should be removed, changed or retained.

# Source comparison 1

## Scope and method

I read the complete draft and the complete supplied Swedish brief, source material and boundaries. This report compares claims, attribution, qualifications and implications. It does not review prose quality or mechanics. The material is synthetic and fictional; no external evidence was used. The target language is British English. There are no speech quotations in the draft, so there are no translated-quotation findings. Changes of meaning in unquoted translation are treated as source-support findings.

The commissioning brief establishes the proposed position: “Avsändare är Sanna Ek, talesperson för föreningen Öppna beslut. Tes: kommunstyrelsen bör skjuta upp ett permanent byte till enbart digital bokning av föreningslokaler och först pröva ett halvår med både telefon och webb.” Advocacy and evaluative reasoning expressed in this commissioned voice are distinguished below from assertions about what the documents establish.

## Complete claim accounting

Each row quotes the source in Swedish. Where a sentence contains several claims, the row identifies and accounts for each. Pronoun features are accounted for separately below.

| Draft passage | Source passage in its own words and language | Comparison |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Title: “Lervik needs evidence before ending telephone bookings” | “Skriv en debattartikel för invånarna i fiktiva Lervik.”; “Tes: kommunstyrelsen bör skjuta upp ett permanent byte till enbart digital bokning av föreningslokaler och först pröva ett halvår med både telefon och webb.”; “Någon tidsmätning eller ekonomisk besparingsberäkning finns inte i handlingarna.” | The place is the fictional town in the brief. The need for evidence is the author's advocated conclusion from the missing measurements and the requested postponement. The title does not assert that a termination has already occurred. Supported as advocacy. |
| “The case for removing telephone bookings from Lervik’s association premises rests on avoiding duplicate administration.” | “Tjänsteutlåtandet inför kommunstyrelsens möte den 18 juni föreslår att telefonbokning tas bort för alla sju lokaler från september. Motivet i utlåtandet är att personalen ska slippa föra in uppgifter i två flöden.”; “Förvaltningens verkliga invändning mot att behålla båda kanalerna är dubbel administration, inte att telefonanvändare är lata eller dyra.” | Same proposal and administrative motive; “rests on” attributes the case to the supplied motive, without adding a demonstrated benefit. “Lervik’s association premises” identifies the municipal debate’s premises. No finding. |
| “But the papers provide no measurement of staff time or calculated savings.” | “Någon tidsmätning eller ekonomisk besparingsberäkning finns inte i handlingarna.” | The explicit absence in the papers is preserved. “Staff time” is the contextual time expenditure of the booking administration. The source specifies financial savings; “calculated savings” in this introduction is less explicit, but the body expressly supplies “financial savings”, and the ordinary contextual reading is monetary savings. No defensible source-support finding in the complete draft. |
| “The municipal executive board should establish what each route costs and why people use it.” | “Under försöket ska förvaltningen registrera tidsåtgång per bokningsväg och be användarna frivilligt ange varför de väljer telefon eller webb.”; “Hon menar att kommunen först måste kunna väga arbetskostnaden mot värdet för användarna.” | An advocated evidential requirement, based on the planned time recording, voluntary reasons and cost comparison. It does not assert that the association already knows either route’s cost. The introduction does not describe the collection method; the body preserves voluntariness. No finding. |
| “By Sanna Ek, spokesperson for Öppna beslut” | “Avsändare är Sanna Ek, talesperson för föreningen Öppna beslut.” | Same named person, role and represented association. No finding. |
| “A staff report for the 18 June meeting of Lervik’s municipal executive board proposes ending telephone booking at all seven premises for local associations from September.” | “Tjänsteutlåtandet inför kommunstyrelsens möte den 18 juni föreslår att telefonbokning tas bort för alla sju lokaler från september.”; the preceding paragraph identifies the subject as “föreningslokaler”. | “Staff report” appropriately names the administrative statement. Meeting date, proposal modality, seven-premises scope and September start are preserved. ### F1: The heading turns an unreported matter into a pilot finding

**Draft:** “The pilot leaves users’ reasons unanswered”.

**Source:** “Den mäter inte ålder, funktionsförmåga eller digital vana.” The proposed later procedure is “be användarna frivilligt ange varför de väljer telefon eller webb”. Sanna’s supported position is “Det är ett skäl att ta reda på varför telefonen fortfarande används.” That position supports an inquiry, not a factual description of all the pilot’s contents.

**Difference:** Scope and state of knowledge. The source specifies three measurements not made and says why further inquiry is advocated. The heading asserts the outcome/content of the pilot in relation to users’ reasons.

**Concrete case:** The pilot could have recorded telephone users’ stated reasons in an open comments field, while measuring none of age, functional ability or digital familiarity. Its report could explain those reasons, and the association could still advocate collecting reasons in a wider trial. Every supplied statement would remain true, but the heading would fail. No supplied passage excludes that case.

**Reverse-direction check:** A pilot without any reasons data but with measured ages would leave reasons unanswered while violating the source’s actual omission statement. This case is excluded by “Den mäter inte ålder, funktionsförmåga eller digital vana.” It therefore provides no independent reverse finding. **Source:** “telefonbokning tas bort för alla sju lokaler från september”, in a source describing “föreningslokaler”.

**Difference:** The draft adds the geographical/organisational qualification “local” to the associations served by the premises. The source identifies association premises but does not identify the associations as local or state their eligibility.

**Concrete case, source holds and draft fails:** The seven premises could be available to national membership associations or visiting national federations while local associations are not eligible to book them. They would still be “föreningslokaler”, and all the dates, counts, pilot procedure and proposed board action would remain as supplied. They would not be premises for local associations. No supplied statement excludes that case; addressing the town’s residents does not establish who may book its premises.

**Reverse-direction check:** Premises for local associations are also association premises in this context. I can name no compatible case in which the draft’s association-purpose description holds but the source’s generic association-purpose description fails. The unsupported narrowing is the finding.

**Smallest supported repair:** Replace “all seven premises for local associations” with “all seven association premises”.

### F3: The comparison changes labour cost into work/effort

**Draft:** “the board should be able to weigh the work involved against the value for users”.

**Source:** “Hon menar att kommunen först måste kunna väga arbetskostnaden mot värdet för användarna.”

**Difference:** The thing to be assessed is changed. “Arbetskostnaden” names the cost of labour; “the work involved” names the work, effort or burden itself. In a source that separately names financial savings and an unresolved trial cost, these are not interchangeable. The user-value side of the comparison and its priority are correctly preserved.

**Concrete case, source requirement satisfied but draft requirement not necessarily satisfied:** The board could compare calculated paid labour cost for the two routes with user value without assessing how demanding or onerous staff find the work. It would have the cost comparison Sanna requires but not necessarily an assessment of “the work involved” in the draft’s broader effort sense. A comparison can price task time without assessing the qualitative work burden. Nothing in the source excludes this distinction.

**Concrete case, draft requirement satisfied but source requirement not satisfied:** The board could assess the additional tasks, effort and time alongside users’ convenience, while leaving wages, staffing costs and the monetary cost of that labour unknown. That would permit weighing “the work involved”, but would not establish “arbetskostnaden”. It is compatible with Sanna having the supplied stance and with the present documents lacking measurements; her stance need not already have been fulfilled. No supplied statement says work burden and paid labour cost are identical.

**Smallest supported repair:** Replace “the work involved” with “the labour cost”: “the board should be able to weigh the labour cost against the value for users.”

# Lervik needs evidence before ending telephone bookings

The case for removing telephone bookings from Lervik’s association premises rests on avoiding duplicate administration. But the papers provide no measurement of staff time or calculated savings. The municipal executive board should establish what each route costs and why people use it.

By Sanna Ek, spokesperson for Öppna beslut

A staff report for the 18 June meeting of Lervik’s municipal executive board proposes ending telephone booking at all seven association premises from September. Öppna beslut wants that permanent switch postponed while both telephone and web booking are tested for six months. I do not oppose digital booking; I question whether the evidence justifies removing the alternative.

## The pilot figures leave users’ reasons unanswered

The municipality’s pilot report, Booking Association Premises, dated 8 April 2026, records 96 web bookings and 24 telephone bookings during an eight-week trial at two venues. Those figures describe bookings, not unique individuals.

It did not measure age, functional ability or familiarity with digital technology. We cannot use the telephone bookings to calculate how many residents cannot book online. A booking made by telephone proves no inability to use the web; it gives us a reason to ask why that route is still used.

## Duplicate administration deserves a fair assessment

The administration wants staff to avoid entering information through two workflows. That objection deserves to be taken seriously. Its case concerns duplicate administration, not a claim that telephone users are lazy or costly.

Yet the papers contain neither a measurement of staff time nor a calculation of financial savings. Before making a permanent change, the board should be able to weigh the labour cost against the value for users. The pilot’s booking totals cannot settle that judgement.

## A wider trial can inform the decision

Our proposal covers all seven venues for six months, keeping both booking routes.

Staff would record the time spent on each route and ask users to explain their choice voluntarily. This would help the board assess both the workload and users’ reasons.

## The board should postpone the permanent switch

Öppna beslut makes no claim to have funded or costed the trial. The executive board must consider its cost, postpone the permanent switch and first test both routes. It can then decide whether a booking channel should be removed, changed or retained.

## Source-support findings and bidirectional cases

### F1 — The absent digital variable changes

**Draft:** “It did not measure age, functional ability or familiarity with digital technology.”

**Source:** “Den mäter inte ålder, funktionsförmåga eller digital vana.”

**Difference:** The draft turns a statement about absent measurement of digital experience/practice into a statement about absent measurement of familiarity with digital technology. The latter can concern recognising technology or knowing what it is, without using it. The relevant factual assertion is the absence of that measurement, not the author's view of its importance.

**Source true, draft false:** The report includes a test asking whether participants recognise a QR code and know what an online authentication system does. That measures familiarity with digital technology. It includes no measure of whether or how regularly participants use digital services, so it does not measure “digital vana”. The supplied source excludes measurements of age, functional ability and digital experience; it contains no statement excluding a technology-recognition measure. This case therefore stands.

**Draft true, source false:** A hypothetical report measures the frequency of completing a fixed digital booking routine, thereby measuring digital practice, but includes no assessment of recognition or knowledge of digital technology more generally. The altered draft could accurately say no such familiarity measure exists, while the source’s exclusion of digital practice would fail. This reverse case illustrates the changed variable; it is necessarily excluded by the supplied statement “Den mäter inte … digital vana” and is not a second defect attributed to the actual source.

**Smallest supported repair:** Replace “familiarity with digital technology” with “experience of using digital tools”. Preserve the other two measured variables and the report-scoped absence.

**Classification:** Source-support finding caused by a changed meaning outside quoted speech. There is no translated-quotation finding.

### F2 — An excluded proportion becomes an excluded count

**Draft:** “We cannot use the telephone bookings to calculate how many residents cannot book online.”

**Source:** “Telefonbokningarna kan därför inte användas för att säga hur stor andel av invånarna som inte kan boka digitalt.” Relevant preceding qualifications: “Rapporten räknar bokningar, inte unika personer. Den mäter inte ålder, funktionsförmåga eller digital vana.” Sanna’s distinct point is: “Att en bokning går via telefon är inte ett bevis för att någon inte kan använda webben.”

**Difference:** “Hur stor andel” is a proportion, whereas “how many” reads as an absolute count. A missing population denominator can prevent a proportion without preventing an absolute count. The source also names inability to book digitally; the draft names inability to book online. The web is the discussed digital route, but using the source’s own term avoids expanding this separate population assertion.

**Source true, draft false:** In a compatible situation, the 24 telephone bookings are known through a separate one-booking-per-participant trial protocol to belong to 24 different residents who cannot complete the web booking process. The report itself still counts bookings, rather than reporting a unique-person count; the protocol and direct knowledge of those participants’ booking ability are not measurements of age, functional ability or digital experience. No resident-population denominator is established. The bookings, with that protocol, can yield an absolute number for these residents while they cannot yield their proportion of the municipality’s residents. A telephone booking by itself remains no proof of web inability, as Sanna says; the protocol and separately established inability supply that information. None of the supplied statements says that there is no such protocol, no ancillary booking-ability information or no way to derive a count; they specify the report’s counting unit, three unmeasured variables and the prohibited proportion inference. This case is sufficient to show that the draft’s broader negative has not been established.

**Draft true, source false:** If an independently known prevalence rate establishes a proportion of residents unable to book digitally but the total resident population is unknown, an absolute count may remain unavailable. That establishes that the count and proportion claims are not interchangeable in the opposite direction. Any version of this case in which the telephone bookings themselves establish the proportion is excluded for this material by “Telefonbokningarna kan därför inte användas för att säga hur stor andel …”. No such information is attributed to the actual source.

**Smallest supported repair:** “We cannot use the telephone bookings to calculate what proportion of residents cannot book digitally.” This preserves the source’s precise object and the warranted certainty of the exclusion. Keep the next sentence’s separate, expressly supplied observation that a telephone booking does not prove inability to use the web.

**Classification:** Source-support finding caused by changed measurement scope outside quoted speech. There is no translated-quotation finding.

## Completion status

Complete: the whole draft, including title, standfirst, byline, headings, factual implications and pronoun features, has been compared with the full supplied brief and source. No speech quotations require a separate quotation-translation assessment. No general editorial or mechanical review was performed.

Unresolved findings: F1 (digital-experience measurement becomes technology familiarity) and F2 (a proportion becomes an absolute count). This report does not modify the draft or source.

### F1: The heading turns an unreported matter into a pilot finding

**Draft:** “The pilot leaves users’ reasons unanswered”.

**Source:** “Den mäter inte ålder, funktionsförmåga eller digital vana.” The proposed later procedure is “be användarna frivilligt ange varför de väljer telefon eller webb”. **Difference:** Scope and state of knowledge. The source specifies three measurements not made and says why further inquiry is advocated. The heading asserts the outcome/content of the pilot in relation to users’ reasons.

**Concrete case:** The pilot could have recorded telephone users’ stated reasons in an open comments field, while measuring none of age, functional ability or digital familiarity. Its report could explain those reasons, and the association could still advocate collecting reasons in a wider trial. Every supplied statement would remain true, but the heading would fail. No supplied passage excludes that case.

**Reverse-direction check:** A pilot without any reasons data but with measured ages would leave reasons unanswered while violating the source’s actual omission statement. **Source:** “telefonbokning tas bort för alla sju lokaler från september”, in a source describing “föreningslokaler”.

**Difference:** The draft adds the geographical/organisational qualification “local” to the associations served by the premises. The source identifies association premises but does not identify the associations as local or state their eligibility.

**Concrete case, source holds and draft fails:** The seven premises could be available to national membership associations or visiting national federations while local associations are not eligible to book them. They would still be “föreningslokaler”, and all the dates, counts, pilot procedure and proposed board action would remain as supplied. They would not be premises for local associations. No supplied statement excludes that case; addressing the town’s residents does not establish who may book its premises.

**Reverse-direction check:** Premises for local associations are also association premises in this context. I can name no compatible case in which the draft’s association-purpose description holds but the source’s generic association-purpose description fails. The unsupported narrowing is the finding.

**Smallest supported repair:** Replace “all seven premises for local associations” with “all seven association premises”.

### F3: The comparison changes labour cost into work/effort

**Draft:** “the board should be able to weigh the work involved against the value for users”.

**Source:** “Hon menar att kommunen först måste kunna väga arbetskostnaden mot värdet för användarna.”

**Difference:** The thing to be assessed is changed. “Arbetskostnaden” names the cost of labour; “the work involved” names the work, effort or burden itself. In a source that separately names financial savings and an unresolved trial cost, these are not interchangeable. The user-value side of the comparison and its priority are correctly preserved.

**Concrete case, source requirement satisfied but draft requirement not necessarily satisfied:** The board could compare calculated paid labour cost for the two routes with user value without assessing how demanding or onerous staff find the work. It would have the cost comparison Sanna requires but not necessarily an assessment of “the work involved” in the draft’s broader effort sense. A comparison can price task time without assessing the qualitative work burden. Nothing in the source excludes this distinction.

**Concrete case, draft requirement satisfied but source requirement not satisfied:** The board could assess the additional tasks, effort and time alongside users’ convenience, while leaving wages, staffing costs and the monetary cost of that labour unknown. That would permit weighing “the work involved”, but would not establish “arbetskostnaden”. It is compatible with Sanna having the supplied stance and with the present documents lacking measurements; her stance need not already have been fulfilled. No supplied statement says work burden and paid labour cost are identical.

**Smallest supported repair:** Replace “the work involved” with “the labour cost”: “the board should be able to weigh the labour cost against the value for users.”

# Lervik needs evidence before ending telephone bookings

The case for removing telephone bookings from Lervik’s association premises rests on avoiding duplicate administration. But the papers provide no measurement of staff time or calculated savings. The municipal executive board should establish what each route costs and why people use it.

By Sanna Ek, spokesperson for Öppna beslut

A staff report for the 18 June meeting of Lervik’s municipal executive board proposes ending telephone booking at all seven association premises from September. Öppna beslut wants that permanent switch postponed while both telephone and web booking are tested for six months. I do not oppose digital booking; I question whether the evidence justifies removing the alternative.

## The pilot figures leave users’ reasons unanswered

The municipality’s pilot report, Booking Association Premises, dated 8 April 2026, records 96 web bookings and 24 telephone bookings during an eight-week trial at two venues. Those figures describe bookings, not unique individuals.

It did not measure age, functional ability or familiarity with digital technology. We cannot use the telephone bookings to calculate how many residents cannot book online. A booking made by telephone proves no inability to use the web; it gives us a reason to ask why that route is still used.

## Duplicate administration deserves a fair assessment

The administration wants staff to avoid entering information through two workflows. That objection deserves to be taken seriously. Its case concerns duplicate administration, not a claim that telephone users are lazy or costly.

Yet the papers contain neither a measurement of staff time nor a calculation of financial savings. Before making a permanent change, the board should be able to weigh the labour cost against the value for users. The pilot’s booking totals cannot settle that judgement.

## A wider trial can inform the decision

Our proposal covers all seven venues for six months, keeping both booking routes.

Staff would record the time spent on each route and ask users to explain their choice voluntarily. This would help the board assess both the workload and users’ reasons.

## The board should postpone the permanent switch

Öppna beslut makes no claim to have funded or costed the trial. The executive board must consider its cost, postpone the permanent switch and first test both routes. It can then decide whether a booking channel should be removed, changed or retained.

Den mäter inte ålder, funktionsförmåga eller digital vana.” Also: “Någon tidsmätning eller ekonomisk besparingsberäkning finns inte i handlingarna.” The judgement is the immediately preceding labour-cost/user-value comparison. The author reasons from the defined limits of booking counts and the absent cost measurement. She does not claim that the report is devoid of evidence of every kind. Supported argument.

26. **Heading: “A wider trial can inform the decision”.** Source: “Öppna beslut föreslår ett sex månader långt försök i alla sju lokaler, med båda bokningsvägarna kvar. Under försöket ska förvaltningen registrera tidsåtgång per bokningsväg och be användarna frivilligt ange varför de väljer telefon eller webb.” “Wider” has an explicit comparator: two pilot premises versus all seven. “Can inform” is the advocated trial’s prospective use, not a claim that a causal effect has already been demonstrated. Supported argument.

27. **“Our proposal covers all seven venues for six months, keeping both booking routes.”** Source: “Öppna beslut föreslår ett sex månader långt försök i alla sju lokaler, med båda bokningsvägarna kvar.” Organisation, seven-premises coverage, six-month duration and retention of both routes are preserved. “Our” is the spokesperson’s institutional voice. Supported.

28. **“Staff would record the time spent on each route”.** Source: “Under försöket ska förvaltningen registrera tidsåtgång per bokningsväg”. Administration acting through staff is compatible with the specified recording work and the source’s earlier “personalen”. The draft’s conditional presents what the proposed trial would entail, preserving the fact that it has not been adopted. Same unit: time by route. Supported.

29. **“and ask users to explain their choice voluntarily.”** Source: “Under försöket ska förvaltningen registrera tidsåtgång per bokningsväg och be användarna frivilligt ange varför de väljer telefon eller webb.” The scope “under försöket” continues from the proposed trial. The choice is between the same two stated routes. Voluntariness modifies the users’ explanation, not the staff’s recording duty. Supported.

30. **“This would help the board assess both the workload and users’ reasons.”** Source: “Under försöket ska förvaltningen registrera tidsåtgång per bokningsväg och be användarna frivilligt ange varför de väljer telefon eller webb.” Also: “Hon menar att kommunen först måste kunna väga arbetskostnaden mot värdet för användarna.” This is the author’s stated purpose for collecting precisely those records and reasons. It claims prospective informational help, without promising a particular outcome or asserting a measured causal effect. Supported argument.

31. **Heading: “The board should postpone the permanent switch”.** Source: “Tes: kommunstyrelsen bör skjuta upp ett permanent byte till enbart digital bokning av föreningslokaler och först pröva ett halvår med både telefon och webb.” The actor, permanence and requested decision are preserved. Supported advocacy.

32. **“Öppna beslut makes no claim to have funded or costed the trial.”** Source: “Föreningen gör inget anspråk på att ha finansierat eller kostnadsberäknat försöket.” This accurately reports the limits of the organisation’s claims. It does not assert that funding or costing never occurred. Supported.

33. **“The executive board must consider its cost”.** Source: “Kostnaden behöver kommunstyrelsen ta ställning till.” This retains cost as an unresolved matter requiring the board’s consideration. “Its” refers to the proposed trial, as in the immediately preceding source sentence. No amount, funding source or affordability assessment is invented. Supported.

34. **“postpone the permanent switch and first test both routes.”** Source: “Tes: kommunstyrelsen bör skjuta upp ett permanent byte till enbart digital bokning av föreningslokaler och först pröva ett halvår med både telefon och webb.” The modal “must” is the author’s advocated obligation, not a purported statutory requirement. The source expressly permits a sharp position and forbids invented legal requirements; this passage states the position. Supported.

35. **“It can then decide whether a booking channel should be removed, changed or retained.”** Source: “Kostnaden behöver kommunstyrelsen ta ställning till. Därefter kan den avgöra om en kanal ska tas bort, ändras eller behållas.” Read with the brief’s “först pröva ett halvår med både telefon och webb”, the draft’s “then” comes after considering the trial cost and testing both routes. All three possible channel decisions remain available. The draft does not promise that telephone will be permanently retained or that a channel must be removed. Supported.

Referent identification and person/number/gender are assessed separately below. English institutional “it/its” marks no natural gender. Swedish common/neuter grammatical gender is not treated as evidence of a human’s sex or gender.

Source plural “användarna” supports plurality. |
| “that permanent switch” | “ett permanent byte till enbart digital bokning”. | Singular demonstrative. | No natural gender. Swedish “ett” is grammatical neuter only. |

## Source-support findings and bidirectional cases

### F1 — The absent digital variable changes

**Draft:** “It did not measure age, functional ability or familiarity with digital technology.”

**Source:** “Den mäter inte ålder, funktionsförmåga eller digital vana.”

**Difference:** The draft turns a statement about absent measurement of digital experience/practice into a statement about absent measurement of familiarity with digital technology. The latter can concern recognising technology or knowing what it is, without using it. The relevant factual assertion is the absence of that measurement, not the author's view of its importance.

**Source true, draft false:** The report includes a test asking whether participants recognise a QR code and know what an online authentication system does. That measures familiarity with digital technology. It includes no measure of whether or how regularly participants use digital services, so it does not measure “digital vana”. The supplied source excludes measurements of age, functional ability and digital experience; it contains no statement excluding a technology-recognition measure. This case therefore stands.

**Draft true, source false:** A hypothetical report measures the frequency of completing a fixed digital booking routine, thereby measuring digital practice, but includes no assessment of recognition or knowledge of digital technology more generally. The altered draft could accurately say no such familiarity measure exists, while the source’s exclusion of digital practice would fail. This reverse case illustrates the changed variable; it is necessarily excluded by the supplied statement “Den mäter inte … digital vana” and is not a second defect attributed to the actual source.

**Smallest supported repair:** Replace “familiarity with digital technology” with “experience of using digital tools”. Preserve the other two measured variables and the report-scoped absence.

**Classification:** Source-support finding caused by a changed meaning outside quoted speech. There is no translated-quotation finding.

### F2 — An excluded proportion becomes an excluded count

**Draft:** “We cannot use the telephone bookings to calculate how many residents cannot book online.”

**Source:** “Telefonbokningarna kan därför inte användas för att säga hur stor andel av invånarna som inte kan boka digitalt.” Relevant preceding qualifications: “Rapporten räknar bokningar, inte unika personer. Den mäter inte ålder, funktionsförmåga eller digital vana.” Sanna’s distinct point is: “Att en bokning går via telefon är inte ett bevis för att någon inte kan använda webben.”

**Difference:** “Hur stor andel” is a proportion, whereas “how many” reads as an absolute count. A missing population denominator can prevent a proportion without preventing an absolute count. The source also names inability to book digitally; the draft names inability to book online. The web is the discussed digital route, but using the source’s own term avoids expanding this separate population assertion.

**Source true, draft false:** In a compatible situation, the 24 telephone bookings are known through a separate one-booking-per-participant trial protocol to belong to 24 different residents who cannot complete the web booking process. The report itself still counts bookings, rather than reporting a unique-person count; the protocol and direct knowledge of those participants’ booking ability are not measurements of age, functional ability or digital experience. No resident-population denominator is established. The bookings, with that protocol, can yield an absolute number for these residents while they cannot yield their proportion of the municipality’s residents. A telephone booking by itself remains no proof of web inability, as Sanna says; the protocol and separately established inability supply that information. None of the supplied statements says that there is no such protocol, no ancillary booking-ability information or no way to derive a count; they specify the report’s counting unit, three unmeasured variables and the prohibited proportion inference. This case is sufficient to show that the draft’s broader negative has not been established.

**Draft true, source false:** If an independently known prevalence rate establishes a proportion of residents unable to book digitally but the total resident population is unknown, an absolute count may remain unavailable. That establishes that the count and proportion claims are not interchangeable in the opposite direction. Any version of this case in which the telephone bookings themselves establish the proportion is excluded for this material by “Telefonbokningarna kan därför inte användas för att säga hur stor andel …”. No such information is attributed to the actual source.

**Smallest supported repair:** “We cannot use the telephone bookings to calculate what proportion of residents cannot book digitally.” This preserves the source’s precise object and the warranted certainty of the exclusion. Keep the next sentence’s separate, expressly supplied observation that a telephone booking does not prove inability to use the web.

**Classification:** Source-support finding caused by changed measurement scope outside quoted speech. There is no translated-quotation finding.

## Completion status

Complete: the whole draft, including title, standfirst, byline, headings, factual implications and pronoun features, has been compared with the full supplied brief and source. No speech quotations require a separate quotation-translation assessment. No general editorial or mechanical review was performed.

Unresolved findings: F1 (digital-experience measurement becomes technology familiarity) and F2 (a proportion becomes an absolute count). This report does not modify the draft or source.

**Draft:** “It did not measure age, functional ability or familiarity with digital technology.”

**Source:** “Den mäter inte ålder, funktionsförmåga eller digital vana.”

**Difference:** The draft turns a statement about absent measurement of digital experience/practice into a statement about absent measurement of familiarity with digital technology. **Source true, draft false:** The report includes a test asking whether participants recognise a QR code and know what an online authentication system does. That measures familiarity with digital technology. It includes no measure of whether or how regularly participants use digital services, so it does not measure “digital vana”. The supplied source excludes measurements of age, functional ability and digital experience; it contains no statement excluding a technology-recognition measure. This case therefore stands.

**Draft true, source false:** A hypothetical report measures the frequency of completing a fixed digital booking routine, thereby measuring digital practice, but includes no assessment of recognition or knowledge of digital technology more generally. The altered draft could accurately say no such familiarity measure exists, while the source’s exclusion of digital practice would fail. This reverse case illustrates the changed variable; it is necessarily excluded by the supplied statement “Den mäter inte … digital vana” and is not a second defect attributed to the actual source.

**Classification:** Source-support finding caused by a changed meaning outside quoted speech. There is no translated-quotation finding.

### F2 — An excluded proportion becomes an excluded count

**Draft:** “We cannot use the telephone bookings to calculate how many residents cannot book online.”

**Source:** “Telefonbokningarna kan därför inte användas för att säga hur stor andel av invånarna som inte kan boka digitalt.” Relevant preceding qualifications: “Rapporten räknar bokningar, inte unika personer. **Difference:** “Hur stor andel” is a proportion, whereas “how many” reads as an absolute count. A missing population denominator can prevent a proportion without preventing an absolute count. The source also names inability to book digitally; the draft names inability to book online. The web is the discussed digital route, but using the source’s own term avoids expanding this separate population assertion.

**Source true, draft false:** In a compatible situation, the 24 telephone bookings are known through a separate one-booking-per-participant trial protocol to belong to 24 different residents who cannot complete the web booking process. The report itself still counts bookings, rather than reporting a unique-person count; the protocol and direct knowledge of those participants’ booking ability are not measurements of age, functional ability or digital experience. No resident-population denominator is established. The bookings, with that protocol, can yield an absolute number for these residents while they cannot yield their proportion of the municipality’s residents. A telephone booking by itself remains no proof of web inability, as Sanna says; the protocol and separately established inability supply that information. None of the supplied statements says that there is no such protocol, no ancillary booking-ability information or no way to derive a count; they specify the report’s counting unit, three unmeasured variables and the prohibited proportion inference. This case is sufficient to show that the draft’s broader negative has not been established.

**Draft true, source false:** If an independently known prevalence rate establishes a proportion of residents unable to book digitally but the total resident population is unknown, an absolute count may remain unavailable. That establishes that the count and proportion claims are not interchangeable in the opposite direction. Any version of this case in which the telephone bookings themselves establish the proportion is excluded for this material by “Telefonbokningarna kan därför inte användas för att säga hur stor andel …”. No such information is attributed to the actual source.

**Smallest supported repair:** “We cannot use the telephone bookings to calculate what proportion of residents cannot book digitally.” This preserves the source’s precise object and the warranted certainty of the exclusion. Keep the next sentence’s separate, expressly supplied observation that a telephone booking does not prove inability to use the web.

**Classification:** Source-support finding caused by changed measurement scope outside quoted speech. There is no translated-quotation finding.

## Source-support findings and bidirectional cases

### F1 — The absent digital variable changes

**Draft:** “It did not measure age, functional ability or familiarity with digital technology.”

**Source:** “Den mäter inte ålder, funktionsförmåga eller digital vana.”

**Difference:** The draft turns a statement about absent measurement of digital experience/practice into a statement about absent measurement of familiarity with digital technology. The latter can concern recognising technology or knowing what it is, without using it. The relevant factual assertion is the absence of that measurement, not the author's view of its importance.

**Source true, draft false:** The report includes a test asking whether participants recognise a QR code and know what an online authentication system does. That measures familiarity with digital technology. It includes no measure of whether or how regularly participants use digital services, so it does not measure “digital vana”. The supplied source excludes measurements of age, functional ability and digital experience; it contains no statement excluding a technology-recognition measure. This case therefore stands.

**Draft true, source false:** A hypothetical report measures the frequency of completing a fixed digital booking routine, thereby measuring digital practice, but includes no assessment of recognition or knowledge of digital technology more generally. The altered draft could accurately say no such familiarity measure exists, while the source’s exclusion of digital practice would fail. This reverse case illustrates the changed variable; it is necessarily excluded by the supplied statement “Den mäter inte … digital vana” and is not a second defect attributed to the actual source.

**Smallest supported repair:** Replace “familiarity with digital technology” with “experience of using digital tools”. Preserve the other two measured variables and the report-scoped absence.

**Classification:** Source-support finding caused by a changed meaning outside quoted speech. There is no translated-quotation finding.

### F2 — An excluded proportion becomes an excluded count

**Draft:** “We cannot use the telephone bookings to calculate how many residents cannot book online.”

**Source:** “Telefonbokningarna kan därför inte användas för att säga hur stor andel av invånarna som inte kan boka digitalt.” Relevant preceding qualifications: “Rapporten räknar bokningar, inte unika personer. Den mäter inte ålder, funktionsförmåga eller digital vana.” Sanna’s distinct point is: “Att en bokning går via telefon är inte ett bevis för att någon inte kan använda webben.”

**Difference:** “Hur stor andel” is a proportion, whereas “how many” reads as an absolute count. A missing population denominator can prevent a proportion without preventing an absolute count. The source also names inability to book digitally; the draft names inability to book online. The web is the discussed digital route, but using the source’s own term avoids expanding this separate population assertion.

**Source true, draft false:** In a compatible situation, the 24 telephone bookings are known through a separate one-booking-per-participant trial protocol to belong to 24 different residents who cannot complete the web booking process. The report itself still counts bookings, rather than reporting a unique-person count; the protocol and direct knowledge of those participants’ booking ability are not measurements of age, functional ability or digital experience. No resident-population denominator is established. The bookings, with that protocol, can yield an absolute number for these residents while they cannot yield their proportion of the municipality’s residents. A telephone booking by itself remains no proof of web inability, as Sanna says; the protocol and separately established inability supply that information. None of the supplied statements says that there is no such protocol, no ancillary booking-ability information or no way to derive a count; they specify the report’s counting unit, three unmeasured variables and the prohibited proportion inference. This case is sufficient to show that the draft’s broader negative has not been established.

**Draft true, source false:** If an independently known prevalence rate establishes a proportion of residents unable to book digitally but the total resident population is unknown, an absolute count may remain unavailable. That establishes that the count and proportion claims are not interchangeable in the opposite direction. Any version of this case in which the telephone bookings themselves establish the proportion is excluded for this material by “Telefonbokningarna kan därför inte användas för att säga hur stor andel …”. No such information is attributed to the actual source.

**Smallest supported repair:** “We cannot use the telephone bookings to calculate what proportion of residents cannot book digitally.” This preserves the source’s precise object and the warranted certainty of the exclusion. Keep the next sentence’s separate, expressly supplied observation that a telephone booking does not prove inability to use the web.

**Classification:** Source-support finding caused by changed measurement scope outside quoted speech. There is no translated-quotation finding.

Complete: the whole draft, including title, standfirst, byline, headings, factual implications and pronoun features, has been compared with the full supplied brief and source. No speech quotations require a separate quotation-translation assessment. No general editorial or mechanical review was performed.

Unresolved findings: F1 (digital-experience measurement becomes technology familiarity) and F2 (a proportion becomes an absolute count). This report does not modify the draft or source.
